entities.summary:
Pietro del Monte was a Venetian jurist and humanist who played a significant role in shaping the intellectual landscape of Europe during the Late Middle Ages. Born into a family of minor nobility, del Monte received his education at the University of Padua, where he became acquainted with the works of Aristotle and other classical authors. He went on to become a respected canonist and jurist, earning the favor of powerful patrons such as the Pope himself.

Del Monte's contributions to the field of law were instrumental in shaping the development of modern civil law systems. His treatise on the subject, 'De iure gentium et civitatis,' remains one of the most influential works of its kind to this day.

Despite his significant impact on legal scholarship, del Monte's legacy extends far beyond the realm of jurisprudence. As a humanist and patron of the arts, he was instrumental in promoting the work of prominent scholars and artists of his time.

His commitment to education and intellectual pursuits earned him a reputation as one of the most learned men of his era. Del Monte's remarkable life serves as a testament to the enduring power of human curiosity and the importance of preserving knowledge for future generations.
